title: The Biggest Stars
subtitle: Monsters of light
yt_title: A Star Bigger Than Saturn's Orbit 🔴 | Ep. 57 #shorts
description:
Episode 57 of a daily journey through the universe. 🔴
The biggest stars: red supergiants like Stephenson 2-18 and UY Scuti may be more than a thousand times wider than the Sun (size estimates are uncertain), and the heaviest known star, R136a1, is about 200 times the Sun's mass.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 58: Next stop, gravitational waves. Ripples in space itself.
Start from Episode 1 "Leaving Earth" on the channel.
Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

Images: NASA (public domain)
Narration: AI voice

#space #biggeststar #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: Episode fifty-seven. Next stop... the biggest stars in the universe.
Our Sun is huge. About one point three million Earths could fit inside. But in the universe, it's ordinary.
segments.headline: The Sun is ordinary

segments.text: Remember Betelgeuse from episode fifteen? If it replaced our Sun, it would reach past the orbit of Mars.
segments.headline: Betelgeuse

segments.text: But some stars are even bigger. One of the largest known is called Stephenson two-eighteen.
segments.headline: Stephenson 2-18

segments.text: Some estimates make it over two thousand times wider than the Sun.
Put it in the center of our solar system, and its surface could reach beyond the orbit of Saturn.
segments.headline: Past Saturn's orbit

segments.text: A plane flying at nine hundred kilometers an hour would need over a thousand years to fly once around it.
Measuring stars this far away is very hard, so these sizes are uncertain. Another giant, U Y Scuti, was once called the biggest.
segments.headline: Sizes are uncertain

segments.text: The heaviest known star is a different one: R one-thirty-six a one, in a nearby galaxy.
segments.headline: R136a1

segments.text: It has about two hundred times the mass of the Sun, and shines millions of times brighter.
Giants like these live fast and die young, in just a few million years, ending as supernovas or black holes.
segments.headline: Live fast, die young

segments.text: Tomorrow, ripples in space itself, detected from a collision a billion light-years away. Next stop: gravitational waves. Follow, so you don't miss episode fifty-eight.
